title: Every reproduction passes on GitHub, and every reading goes through the one command
set_out: Test Met-A against IAM-Atlas v2.1 with the chain's same-run tare on an independent laboratory's healthy cells, and finish the open GitHub runs.
open_at_turnover: Open: Group-A's reproduction through the one command (GRP-004); the human timing sample for the firm rate (PHY-049); information sphere test 11 (ATL-046); the catalogue corrections (no dates in prose, one source per fact).
closing: A long day of making the work replicable: if the chain did not produce it, it did not happen.

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: Met-A against the atlas, tared on the same slide (GRP-014, DEV-METAA-ATLAS-01 exploration 6)
entries.what: An independent laboratory's healthy children's monocytes, read against the atlas's adult monocytes and tared against healthy monocytes run on the same slide: all 67 read Normal, and a planted 1 % loss of their pattern stands out at 3.6 times the healthy spread. Children given BCG at birth read Normal too.
entries.why: Met-A read against the atlas lets any cell type in the atlas be read, not only the ones with a purified-array reference; the same-run tare cancels the laboratory and age gaps.

entries.title: All ten reproductions pass on GitHub's machines (OTH-076)
entries.what: The mouse reproduction ran across 19 GitHub machines and every read set came out identical to the committed run, so every reproduction a researcher can run now passes on GitHub's free machines, without the AWS account. One workflow runs all of them from a researcher's own copy of the repository.
entries.why: A result counts only when someone else can produce it again from the repository alone.

entries.title: The C-Score's band test, rerun through the one command (COM-CSCORE-011)
entries.what: Every reading and tare by run_sample.py from the raw arrays: the band holds again. One array fewer is scored, because Stage 0's bisulfite limit, set after the first scoring, now stops it.
entries.why: Everything is rerun through the one command, so a researcher replicates exactly what we ran.

entries.title: Met-A against the atlas through the one command, two independent monocyte series (GRP-014)
entries.what: Healthy monocytes of two independent laboratories, read against IAM-Atlas v2.1 and tared against healthy monocytes on their own slide, all read Normal, and a planted 1 % loss stands out in both.
entries.why: Met-A against the atlas would let one reference serve every cell type.

entries.title: Every cell in a mix, and one blood draw (GRP-015, GRP-016)
entries.what: The one command now reads every cell type of the atlas in one run, scores Met-A for each cell it finds, reads sequencing values with a read-count correction, and reads a whole blood draw (white cells and plasma) as one record. Nine known mixtures of tissue DNA in blood were found at the right sizes.
entries.why: A single blood draw read for every cell in it is the goal the instruments were built toward.

entries.title: The information sphere, with each site's level taken out (ATL-046)
entries.what: A construction that removes each site's methylation level before the geometry passed its synthetic test; on the real atlas it met two of three checks, and the next test asks the right question with level-matched lines.
entries.why: A map of how sites behave, not where they sit, is the second sphere.

entries.title: Every globe layer has a working slider: the audit after the fix (ATL-063)
entries.what: A browser audit of every layer of every globe on the live site: every layer has a working slider, and every change layer goes dark at the right end on a healthy blood. The release check now tests every layer.
entries.why: A picture a researcher cannot trust is worse than none.

entries.title: The X and Y in IAM-A's held error (OTH-080, DEV-IAMA-SEX-01)
entries.what: Counting IAM-A's held error with the X and Y left out moves IAM-A by a fraction of a percent, well inside the band; the line and band are kept.
entries.why: A reader may assume the X was not handled; this shows it was.

entries.title: Colon's controls matched on the slide (ATL-070, DEV-TISSUE-GLOBE-01 run 3)
entries.what: Matching colon controls on the same slide changes nothing: two healthy people's colon differs nearly as much as a tumor differs from its own normal, which is why the person's own normal tissue is the reference that counts.
entries.why: It says which reference a tissue reading needs.

sections.heading: Our own mistakes, and what caught each

entries.title: Work that called chain pieces instead of the one command (lesson C33)
entries.what: Several tests and pictures called chain stages directly. By the author's rule they do not count; they were withdrawn and are being rerun through run_sample.py, and the push gate now refuses a test script that does not run it.
entries.why: The chain did not produce it, so it did not happen.

entries.title: A test script pushed that did not compile (lesson C36)
entries.what: Seven GitHub runs failed before reading any data; the push gate now compiles every Python file first.
